problems.source: Stoll (2005), Theorem 1.3; JSP-000391 catalog source and pinned source audit.

requirements.description: All integer bases g>=2 and all positive reals (hence positive algebraic reals) with the stated normalization.
The prescribed recurrence produces the actual base-g digits at every index.
Digits lie in the radix range and decoded truncations converge; admissible shifts are nonempty.

problems.source: Erdos problem 547, universal tree Ramsey bound; Erdos-Sos source theorem used for tree-free edge bound.

requirements.description: Every finite tree on n>=2 vertices has the claimed two-colour Ramsey upper bound.
Exact containment means an injective, non-induced graph copy.
Even-order stars attain the bound; separately submitted multicolour extension includes finite nonempty colour sets.

problems.source: Erdos problem 1114; Balint (1960) and Lorch (1963), pp. 307-314, equally spaced polynomial zeros.

requirements.description: Every nonzero real polynomial of degree N+1 with N+1 equally spaced real zeros, with N>0 and positive spacing.
One unique derivative zero lies in each intervening interval.
Derivative gaps increase strictly on the appropriate right half and obey mirror symmetry, including small and central cases.

problems.source: Erdos problem 294; Liu-Sawhney complete reciprocal-sum estimates.

requirements.description: Unit-fraction representability is by a finite increasing sequence of distinct positive denominators bounded by N.
The extremal quantity is the true least positive nonrepresentable denominator.
Both eventual upper and lower estimates, with positive constants and the claimed iterated-log profile, hold uniformly for all sufficiently large N.
Every multiplicity r>=2 and every sufficiently large finite ground type: exact multiplicity r at each occurring level.
An antichain with r(n-3) members exists and one with r(n-2) members does not.
The threshold is the least eventual cutoff; two-sided threshold estimates and ratio limit are proved.

problems.source: https://www.erdosproblems.com/1099 — main divisor-gap existence question; Vose (1984), pp. 233-238.

requirements.description: All real exponents alpha>1, including those arbitrarily close to one.
One positive bound C is uniform over arbitrarily large positive integer witnesses.
The sum includes every adjacent pair of the complete sorted positive divisor list; n=0 is excluded.
The original minimum is over all rational polynomials with a specified number of nonzero terms and is attained.
That actual minimum square-support count tends to infinity.
The submitted sparse family transfers from integers to rationals and gives genuine minimum bounds at arbitrarily large support sizes.

problems.source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1409.5661v1 — Section 1, p. 2, original relative-count question.

requirements.description: Count all sum-free subsets and all inclusion-maximal sum-free subsets of the entire interval, allowing equal summands.
The maximal/all count ratio tends to zero, including a fixed exponential separation.
The claimed all-N lower construction is valid also at small orders; later sharp exponent is not claimed.
One positive absolute constant precedes every finite simple graph on n>=2 vertices.
Clique subdivisions use genuine paths, injective branch vertices and disjoint interiors; the maximum order is attained and positive.
The uniform chromatic/subdivision ratio bound, extremal bound and exact finite Catlin witness consequences have their stated scopes.

problems.source: https://arxiv.org/html/2408.13839v1#S1 — original Erdos-Gimbel question preceding Theorem 1.

requirements.description: The complete full-sequence G(n,1/2) chromatic-minus-cochromatic gap diverges in probability.
Finite graph and colouring minima, rational counting and binomial probability, and subtraction agree exactly.
The full proof does not assume the earlier finite reduction premise; conditional supplement retains its positive-mass and probability-ratio hypotheses.
